description:
The Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2021. 

This scheme is specifically aimed at improving the storage infrastructure for onions. 

Onions are a staple vegetable in Indian households and their prices can fluctuate significantly. 

The volatility in onion prices often affects farmers’ incomes and consumers’ budgets. 

The Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme aims to stabilize these prices by enhancing storage capacities. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance for the construction of onion storage facilities. 

The government has set a target to construct storage facilities that can hold at least 1.5 million metric tons of onions. 

This initiative is expected to benefit over 1 lakh onion farmers across the country. 

The scheme is designed to reduce post-harvest losses which can be as high as 30 percent for onions due to inadequate storage. 

Farmers will receive a subsidy of 50 percent of the total cost incurred for building the storage facilities. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at ₹20 lakh per project. 

This means that if a farmer invests ₹40 lakh in constructing a storage facility, they will receive ₹20 lakh as a subsidy from the government. 

The eligibility criteria for the Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme include being a registered onion farmer. 

Farmers must also be part of a cooperative society or a farmer producer organization. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for this scheme. 

However, farmers must provide proof of their farming activities and registration as onion growers. 

The application process for the scheme is straightforward. 

Farmers must first visit the official website of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

They need to fill out the application form available on the website. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card, land ownership documents, and registration certificates. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the district agriculture officer. 

The review process typically takes about 30 days. 

If approved, the subsidy amount will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The scheme is expected to be implemented in phases. 

The first phase began in 2021 and will continue until 2024. 

Farmers can apply for the subsidy at any time during this period. 

The disbursement of funds will occur quarterly based on the number of applications approved. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

State governments will also play a crucial role in the implementation at the local level. 

The contact details for the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare can be found on their official website. 

Farmers can also reach out to local agricultural offices for assistance with the application process. 

The Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme is part of a broader initiative to enhance the agricultural sector in India. 

The government aims to increase farmers' income by reducing post-harvest losses and ensuring better price stability. 

In addition to storage facilities, the scheme also encourages the use of modern technology in storage practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt scientific storage methods to prolong the shelf life of onions. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It is estimated that the construction of storage facilities will generate around 50,000 jobs. 

The government has allocated ₹1,000 crore for the implementation of this scheme. 

This funding will cover the subsidy amounts as well as administrative costs. 

The Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme is expected to significantly impact the onion supply chain. 

By improving storage facilities, farmers can sell their produce at better prices. 

This will also lead to a more stable supply of onions in the market. 

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

It is also part of the larger strategy to promote sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power in the market. 

The government is also providing training programs on best practices for onion storage. 

These programs are conducted in collaboration with agricultural universities and research institutions. 

Farmers who participate in these training programs can gain valuable insights into modern storage techniques. 

The Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme is a significant step towards empowering onion farmers. 

It aims to create a more resilient agricultural sector that can withstand market fluctuations. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from farmers who have benefited from similar initiatives in the past. 

Overall, the Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna scheme represents a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges faced by onion farmers in India. 

By providing financial assistance and promoting better storage practices, the government aims to enhance the livelihoods of farmers and ensure food security for consumers. 

This scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to supporting the agricultural sector and improving the economic conditions of farmers across the country.
